text_blocks.snippet: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) causes high blood pressure in the lung arteries, making the right side of the heart work too hard to pump blood.
snippet_highlighted_words: high blood pressure in the lung arteries

text_blocks.snippet: In the early stages, PAH may cause no symptoms or mimic other common lung and heart conditions. As the blood vessels in the lungs thicken and narrow, common signs include:

list.snippet: Shortness of breath (dyspnea), especially during physical exertion or climbing stairs
Heart palpitations or a fast, racing heartbeat

text_blocks.snippet: As the strain on the right side of the heart increases and right-sided heart failure develops, additional symptoms often appear:

list.snippet: Swelling (edema) in the ankles, legs, or feet
Swollen abdomen (ascites or fluid retention) from blood backing up toward the liver and kidneys
Fainting spells (syncope), particularly during or after physical activity
Coughing up blood (hemoptysis) in severe cases
Hoarseness caused by an enlarged pulmonary artery pressing on chest nerves

text_blocks.snippet: You can learn more about recognizing warning signs and diagnostic testing via the American Lung Association or review broader risk details from the Mayo Clinic.
If you or someone you know is experiencing these signs, let me know:

list.snippet: Who is experiencing the symptoms (age, general health background)
How long they have been happening or if they are getting worse
What specific activities trigger the shortness of breath or dizziness

text_blocks.snippet: I can provide more context on what steps or specialist evaluations are typically next.
